contradictions.detail: The listing says 'Price includes fees', but the dealer disclaimer says the price 'may exclude taxes, license and title fees and documentary service fee'. Out-the-door terms are ambiguous.

critical_evidence.evidence: CARFAX shows only four service entries in ten years, with reported gaps 2018–2022 and 2022–2025. The latest oil change is 10/16/2026 at the dealer PDI. There is no reported brake fluid flush at any point, though absence of an entry does not prove it was never done. No invoices were provided.

Build date 06/27/2016 per the CARFAX NICB entry places this car in the early ND1 6MT risk window. No transmission repair or warranty replacement entry is reported. A door-jamb build-date photo was not examined here.
Seat and door photos look clean. Footwell carpet, underlay, seat-rail bolts and the soft-top drain area behind the seats were not examined here. The top is down in every photo examined.

CARFAX says 'No open recalls reported to CARFAX', but it shows no recall completion entries. Two campaigns apply to this car: 19V496000 (2016 skid plate/bracket detachment) and 24V695000 (airbag control module software). 19V072000 is automatic-only and does not apply to a manual. No Mazda dealer visit is reported since the 2024 airbag campaign. An NHTSA VIN lookup or Mazda dealer printout is needed.

CARFAX shows tires replaced 04/11/2022 (19,434 mi) and battery replaced 10/16/2026 at the dealer PDI. The listing makes no new-tire claim. Tire DOT date codes are still worth photographing to confirm they match the 2022 entry.

documentation.rationale: Both halves are present but incomplete. On identity: VIN, decode match, guaranteed clean title, a 1-owner history and a consistent odometer trail. On maintenance: CARFAX shows only four service entries in ten years, multi-year gaps, no brake fluid, transmission, diff or coolant entries, no invoices, and no photos of at-risk areas (underside, footwells, top fabric).

condition.rationale: Photos show a clean, stock-looking car with tidy tan leather and unmarked wheels. The dealer PDI replaced the battery and serviced the brakes and oil on 10/16/2026. However, there is no PPI, no underside or engine-bay photos, top fabric not shown up, and no evidence on a 2016-build gearbox.

price_value.rationale: $21,818 sits above the fair value estimate ($17,988–$21,573, mid $19,591), about 11% over the mid. Comparable California soft-top ND1s are listed around $20.5–21k. Catch-up maintenance is also likely.

mission_fit.rationale: A manual roadster with a point of view, highly reliable, easy to resell, and under the $27,000 ceiling, though above the $19,000 ideal. The undocumented early-2016 6MT keeps it from being a decisive fit.

logistics.rationale: Champaign, IL is a long fly-and-drive from Carmel. A dealer seller and a 2016 Mazda make California registration and smog likely straightforward. PPI access before payment is not stated and must be arranged.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Grand Touring with tan leather, gray paint and a 6MT, apparently unmodified and single-owner. A pleasant spec, but it is the ND1 engine and not a standout colour or Club/Brembo car.

ppi_focus: 6MT on a June 2016 build: warm shifts into 2nd and 3rd under load, pop-out on decel, bearing noise, fluid condition
Clutch: engagement height, slip in 4th–6th under load, hydraulic leaks
Underbody corrosion from Illinois salt: subframes, brake and fuel lines, fasteners, rocker seams
Soft top: fabric wear at the rear corners and header, seals, drains behind the seats, footwell dampness, seat-rail bolt corrosion
Water pump weep hole and coolant age and condition; valve cover, front crank seal and rear diff seal seepage
Brake fluid moisture test, plus pad and rotor measurement after the PDI 'brakes serviced'
Paint meter on aluminium hood, trunk and fenders; nose chips; respray evidence despite the clean CARFAX
Recall status check by VIN (skid plate bracket, airbag module software)
Suspension: end links, LCA bushings, damper leaks, alignment readings
Mazda Connect screen ghost-touch test and scan for stored codes
what_would_change_verdict: A price adjustment toward the $19,600 fair value mid would materially improve value
A clean independent PPI with good warm 2nd/3rd shifts, a dry and rust-free underside, and a sound top/drains would lift condition
Recall completion printouts plus owner invoices filling the 2018–2025 gaps would lift documentation
Downward: gearbox grinding or pop-out, significant underbody corrosion, cabin water evidence, or the dealer refusing a PPI
evidence.mission_note: A manual ND roadster is a genuine enthusiast bridge, reliable and easy to resell, and the Miata is back on Jason's list. This one sits above the ideal price band, and its early-2016 gearbox and Illinois history need answers before it is more than plausible.
evidence.rationale: The VIN decode and CARFAX establish a 2016 MX-5 Grand Touring with one personal owner for ten years in Illinois, a guaranteed clean title, no reported accidents, and an odometer trail consistent with the photographed 34,462 miles. The report also documents tire replacement in 04/2022 and a dealer PDI on 10/16/2026 covering oil, air filter, a new battery and brake service. Maintenance documentation is otherwise thin: four service entries in ten years, with no reported entries 2018–2022 or 2022–2025, and no reported brake fluid, transmission, diff or coolant work. That is no reported entry, not proof of neglect. The NICB entry dates the build to June 2016, inside the early ND1 6MT risk window, and there are no transmission records. Recall completion for the skid-plate and airbag campaigns is not shown. Photos show a clean, stock-looking car with tidy tan leather. Underside, top fabric, footwells and engine bay were not examined here. The $21,818 ask is above the fair value estimate of $17,988–$21,573.
evidence.next_action: Ask the dealer for the door-jamb build-date photo, a VIN recall printout, the 10/16/2026 PDI repair order and lift photos of the underside, and confirm they will allow an independent PPI in Champaign before any deposit.
